title: FastPath feature experiments notebook
content:
Context / goal:
Quick, cheap ways to get a feel for feature-level perf & UX tradeoffs for short-context conversations. 'FastPath' is a lightweight feature scaffold (client + middleware + runtime hints) that tries experiments with: trimmed context, prefix caching, and speculative low-fidelity completions.

Top-level hypotheses:
1) A tiny set of heuristics (recent-turn-priority + anchor-sentences) recovers >90% of perceived relevance while cutting average token cost by ~30% on chat workloads.
2) Early speculative low-fidelity responses (short max-tokens, low-temp ensembles) reduce tail latency for users who accept rough responses, with fallback to high-fidelity generation if user asks for clarification.
3) Developer ergonomics: a single SDK flag + two toggleable policies (cost-first vs latency-first) will be sufficient for most product teams to adopt.

Proposed quick experiments (MVP 4 wks):
- E1: Heuristic context sampler (client-side): implement recent-turn-priority + named-anchors. Run A/B in QA playground vs full-context baseline. Metric: perceived relevance (micro-survey), delta token count, latency.
- E2: Speculative short-completions: server side config to attempt a 32-token low-temp output in parallel, deliver if confidence heuristic > threshold; otherwise show streaming high-fidelity result. Metric: tail latency P95, acceptance rate of speculative wins.
- E3: Cost-first autoswitch: policy that quantizes to 8-bit and applies KV cache favouring; measure throughput and quality regressions on eval set.

User stories (short):
- As a mobile product engineer, I want to reduce token spend on high-frequency chats so I can lower infra cost without user-visible regressions.
- As a PM, I want an easy flag to try latency-first behaviour in a beta so we can measure NPS impact.
- As an SRE, I want clear observability (token breakdown per route, fallback counts) to validate rollout safety.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP):
- Built client toggle to enable FastPath sampling and documented SDK usage (one-liner).
- Server returns telemetry for: tokens_saved_estimate, speculative_win, fallback_count per request.
- Quality guardrails: automated micro-eval shows <3% drop in top-1 accuracy on curated prompts.
- Rollout plan: start with internal opt-in (ENG + DS) -> 1 customer beta -> gradual enable by route.

Instrumentation & metrics:
- Primary: tokens_per_session, cost_per_session_est, perceived_relevance_score (micro-survey), p50/p95 latency.
- Safety: speculative_win_rate, fallback_rate, error_rate delta.
- Health: CPU/GPU utilization, queue_depth, avg_batch_size.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How to compute a reliable confidence metric for speculative completions? LM logprob heuristics might be noisy. Consider model ensemble or distillation signal.
- UX: what do we show when speculative result is replaced? toast? inline "improved answer" update? consider short animation to avoid jarring flashes.
- Billing: how to attribute token costs for speculative attempts? double-counting risk. Need finance input.
- Compliance: make sure cached prefixes don't leak PII across sessions. Add opt-out.

Quick implementation sketch:
- Client: sample context -> add header fastpath: {policy: "cost-first"|"latency-first", anchors: [ids]}
- Middleware: route-checker -> attach speculative job to run with short token limit; publish telemetry to trace.
- Runtime: lightweight policy evaluator selects quantization path or full path; fallback route with model variant mapping.

Mini roadmap (dates rough):
- Week 1: wire client flag + local QA harness; basic telemetry.
- Week 2: implement speculative runner; internal dogfood.
- Week 3: micro-evals and tweak confidence threshold; add micro-survey integration.
- Week 4: internal beta + brief docs + roll-out checklist.

To do (personal):
- [ ] Spike on confidence heuristics (logprob-based vs. ensemble). Slack @ml-research.
- [ ] Draft one-pager for PM review (Maya).
- [ ] Add quick demo to playground: toggle on/off, show token delta.

Notes / random ideas (brain dump):
- Could expose an "explainable-sampling" API that returns which anchors were used to compose the prompt to help debugging.
- Consider "grace budgeting" where a session accumulates a small buffer of extra tokens for fallbacks.
- Keep naming simple: 'fastpath' vs 'fastpath-speculative' variant naming in logs.

References / links I keep needing:
- previous context eviction notes: CONFLUENCE-CTX/eviction-playbook
- latency-investigation thread: slack://channels/C0LATENCY/fastpath

Endnote: this is rough. Primary goal for next week is to produce a 1-page decision doc with 2 clear experiments and expected metric deltas. Then get sign-off for internal beta.
